Phase 1a: Basis-Free Spectral Metrics

Gate G1 — At least 1 of 3 proposed metrics shows ≥10% relative difference from aggregate MMD
DECISION: GO — All 12/12 pairs exceed 10%; up to 63× relative gap

Metrics Implemented

Spectral Metrics (proposed)

MetricDefinitionSensitivity
Spectral Density JSDKDE on normalized eigenvalues λi/λmax, Jensen-Shannon divergenceCoarse-grained spectral shape
Quantile-Band Energy (QBE)Equal-mass quantile bands, L2 distance between normalized per-band energyFine-grained spectral fidelity
Heat Kernel Signature (HKS)Tr(exp(−tL)) over 50 log-spaced t, L2 distance of normalized tracesMulti-scale diffusion structure

Standard Metrics (baseline comparison)

MetricDefinition
Degree MMDMMD with RBF kernel on degree distributions
Clustering MMDMMD on local clustering coefficient distributions
Triangle MMDMMD on per-node triangle count distributions

Experimental Design

Reference graphs: SBM(q=0.01), SBM(q=0.1), BA(m=3), BA(m=8)

Baselines (3 types of decreasing spectral fidelity):

  • ER (matched density) — Erdős-Rényi with same edge density. Poor spectral match.
  • Configuration model (matched degree) — Same degree sequence. Good local structure, wrong spectral structure.
  • SBM (approx params) — SBM with heuristically matched parameters. Moderate match.

Total: 12 reference-baseline pairs.

Rank correlation: Spearman ρ = 0.64, p = 0.024 — statistically significant but moderate, confirming the two metric families capture partially independent information.

Spectral Density & HKS Comparisons

Key Findings

1. QBE is the most informative new metric. Quantile-band energy distance consistently produces the largest information gap across all 12 pairs. The clearest case: BA(m=3) vs Configuration model — degree MMD is 0.001 (essentially identical), but QBE distance is 0.260 (63× relative gap). The configuration model preserves degree structure but completely fails to reproduce spectral energy distribution.
2. Spectral JSD is less sensitive at small scales. JSD shows meaningful separation only for large structural differences (SBM vs SBM mismatch). For subtle differences (ER, config model), JSD values are very small (<0.02) because KDE smoothing loses resolution for localized spectral differences.
3. HKS provides complementary signal. HKS distance captures differences at specific diffusion timescales, most informative for SBM pairs where community structure creates characteristic timescale signatures.
4. Standard metrics have blind spots. The configuration model baseline exposes a fundamental blind spot: graphs with identical degree sequences can have vastly different spectral properties. Standard degree/clustering/orbit MMD cannot detect this — validating the core premise of H3.

Evaluation Strategy for Phase 2

  1. QBE distance as primary spectral fidelity metric
  2. HKS distance as complementary multi-scale metric
  3. Spectral JSD for coarse-grained sanity checks
  4. Standard MMD metrics reported for comparability with prior work
